key_reasoning.reason: Four components across three subsystems: a new prompt-cache resolver module with a precedence table (claude/prompt-cache.ts), the Claude agent plugin launch path (claude.plugin.ts, now sharing claudeCacheDefaults and logging the effective setup), the claude-code-otlp settings-layer reader reused as a shared source (claude-settings-env.ts), and a new doctor health check registered in the doctor command (PromptCacheCheck + checks/index + doctor/index). Base L; bumped to XL because shared utilities were touched (terminal-text sanitizer in src/utils, settings-layer reader shared with the OTLP adapter).

No exact precedent for a multi-source precedence resolver (settings env blocks > shell > CodeMie default, then ordered TTL rows); the code itself notes the order is unverified against the Claude Code binary. Doctor prints values from untrusted repo settings files, so terminal-control sanitization was required; an adjacent util (safeTerminalValue) existed and stripTerminalControls was factored from it, so the sanitization floor did not apply. The many edge states (empty settings env entry, unreadable layer, non-object env, unknown switch values, subagent override) are covered by new edge-case test suites. Read-only, trivially reversible.

14 files (diffstat), roughly 6-7 new (prompt-cache.ts, PromptCacheCheck.ts and new test files) and 7-8 modified, spread over src/agents/plugins (claude, claude-code-otlp), src/cli/commands/doctor, src/utils, tests/integration and .ai-run/guides: XL band (11-15).

Checked against project L example profile-provider-decoupling (14 files, total 23): similar file count and multi-subsystem scope, but this change has no persistence/migration layer, so a lower L total of 21 agrees. The initial assessment scored 14 (S); actual work grew well beyond it (a new resolver and a doctor check were added beyond the env-default fix). Borderline 20/21: Technical Risk is L, so the lean-lower rule does not apply.
